blinding_guess.why: Both mesh files exist at the paths their package:// URIs name, are well-formed binary STL (size = 84 + 50*facets) and are metre-scale, so the two resource elements look sound. robot_description is declared, but the top-level xacro (urdf/sda10f.xacro:5) calls <xacro:motoman_sda10f prefix=""/>, and no file in the snapshot defines a macro of that name: sda10f_macro.xacro instantiates the torso and arms directly at <robot> level, so the model only comes out if the xacro in use ignores the undefined call. The command also goes through $(find xacro)/xacro.py. Whether either breaks depends on the xacro release, and ros_distro is null.

notes: ROS 1 package; QoS fields null throughout. param:/robot_description: the code names it relatively as robot_description (copied verbatim into declares); it resolves to /robot_description when load_sda10f.launch is included at the root namespace, as robot_state_visualize_sda10f.launch:27 and test_sda10f.launch:3 do (test/launch_test.xml:35 includes it under ns load_sda10f). It is a URDF string generated by xacro from urdf/sda10f.xacro -> sda10f_macro.xacro -> common_torso_macro.xacro + arm_macro.xacro. It is a parameter, not a message: msg_type is null and definition_id is null (the value is generated from several xacro files, so no single definition file exists to hash). frame null because the description declares a whole link tree (root link base_link) rather than one frame. Units are not stated in code; URDF lengths and angles are used without comment. Resources: the declares templates have no form for resource elements, so I used 'resource <uri>: <SHA-256 of raw file bytes>', by analogy with the msg template; other runs may have chosen a different form. definition_id is null for both meshes because definition_hash.py sha256 reads the file as UTF-8 text and fails on binary STL (UnicodeDecodeError at byte 80).
